lines.speaker: orren_gravetide
lines.text: Magic takes years to learn. A sword takes months. Why do people choose magic?

lines.speaker: bram_coldfire
lines.text: Because after those years, a sword is still just a sword.

lines.speaker: bram_coldfire
lines.text: Your brother — did he believe in the Rift?

lines.speaker: orren_gravetide
lines.text: He believed in what he could see and hit. He would have hated my reading your notes.

lines.speaker: orren_gravetide
lines.text: He was the best of us.

lines.speaker: orren_gravetide
lines.text: You ever fight without the fire? Hands, feet, steel?

lines.speaker: bram_coldfire
lines.text: When the fire won't come. Which is more often than I admit.

lines.speaker: bram_coldfire
lines.text: You act like honor is simple.

lines.speaker: orren_gravetide
lines.text: The concept is simple. Living it is the hard part. I've never pretended otherwise.

lines.speaker: orren_gravetide
lines.text: What drew you to the Rift? Most scholars run from it.

lines.speaker: bram_coldfire
lines.text: The same thing that draws you toward a fight you can't win. Some problems demand to be faced.
